inj.note: Coleman already appeared to make his move last week during a 30-16 win over Arizona, playing 50 percent of snaps on offense while leading the Broncos in carries (nine) and rushing yards (54). Meanwhile, Harvey (25% snap share, five touches) and J.K. Dobbins (21% snap share, six touches) both scored touchdowns despite losing a lot of playing time to Coleman in the rookie's first game back from injured reserve. There's no assurance Coleman's role will continue to grow, but Harvey's upcoming absence -- be it for one game or longer -- does give Coleman a better chance to consolidate rushing and receiving work in Denver's backfield.

news.h: J.K. Dobbins puts team success first
news.d: Jeff Legwold on J.K. Dobbins' workload and his willingness to share carries with Jonah Coleman as long as the Broncos win.
